items.stem: What does [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers(...)] on a POCO declare?

options.text: That more than one source system can own records of this destination entity type
That the entity has more than one destination
That every property must be nullable
That the entity should be garbage-collected aggressively

items.explanation: It registers the several source systems that may each own records of this entity type, so each source's IDs can be mapped to the shared destination records.

misconceptions.b: It's about multiple sources, not multiple destinations.
misconceptions.c: That's the nullable requirement (L0.E2), a separate rule.

items.stem: A School record is fed by both PowerSchool and HR. Why doesn't the destination end up with two School records?

options.text: Each source gets its own mapping to the same destination record, and dedup converges a second source's record onto the existing one instead of duplicating it
The second source is ignored entirely
Synnduit merges the two source databases before syncing
PowerSchool and HR must never feed the same entity

items.explanation: With shared source identifiers, each source has its own mapping (L1.6) to the one destination record; when a second source brings a record the destination already has, dedup (L1.11) matches by [DuplicationKey] and maps to it rather than creating a twin.

misconceptions.b: Both sources contribute; neither is ignored.
misconceptions.d: Co-feeding one entity is exactly what [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] enables.

items.stem: HR is the system of record for staff, but it has no record of Contract Staff. Those are maintained in a JSON file instead. How does Synnduit let JSON be the system of record for just the Contract Staff while HR stays authoritative for everyone else — without duplicating anyone?
rubric: Add JSON (and HR) to the entity's [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] so both sources can own records of the type
Each source gets its own mapping to the destination; ownership is record-level — HR owns its staff, JSON owns the Contract Staff HR lacks
Because the two sources own different (non-overlapping) records, they don't collide; where they could overlap, dedup ([DuplicationKey]) converges rather than duplicates
Result: one destination Staff set, fed by two systems of record, each authoritative for its portion
items.sampleAnswer: List both HR and JSON in the Staff entity's [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers]. That lets each be a system of record for records of the type, each with its own mapping to the shared destination record. Ownership is at the record level: HR remains authoritative for the staff it holds, and JSON becomes the SOR for the Contract Staff HR doesn't have. The two own different records so they don't collide; if they ever did, dedup matches on the [DuplicationKey] and maps to the existing record instead of creating a duplicate. The destination ends up with one staff set fed by two systems of record.

items.stem: The DDH `School` is enriched by several sources — PowerSchool sets the government school code, JSON sets `SiteUrlSuffix`. How do both sources' columns land on the one record without each feed wiping the other's fields?

options.text: [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] converges the sources onto one record; each source sets only its own columns, and by the nullable rule (L0.E2) a source's null on a column it doesn't provide is ignored — so it doesn't overwrite the other source's value
The last source to run wins and overwrites every column
Synnduit keeps a separate copy of the record per source
You must merge the sources into a single feed first

items.explanation: [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] lets multiple sources map to the same destination record; column co-ownership works because unprovided fields arrive null and are ignored by default (L0.E2). Use [ForceNullPropagation] when a source's null on a column it owns should actually take effect. So co-ownership is both by row and by column — this attribute isn't records-only.

misconceptions.b: Unprovided nulls are ignored, not written — each source only affects the columns it owns.
misconceptions.c: There's one converged destination record, not one per source.
misconceptions.d: Each source keeps its own feed; the engine converges them via mappings + dedup.

items.stem: A child record references a Staff by a PowerSchool id, and the run throws 'unable to resolve reference identifier.' The Staff entity's [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] lists HR and JSON but not PowerSchool. What's the fix?

options.text: Add PowerSchool to Staff's [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers] so that source's ids can be mapped

items.explanation: If a source isn't in [SharedSourceSystemIdentifiers], the engine can't map that source's ids for the entity, so a reference by that id can't resolve. Adding the source to the list fixes it (this is the L3.5 exception).

misconceptions.c: Thresholds are unrelated; the issue is an unregistered source system.
